item.title: Re: "How and when to use causal and associational language" and causal associations
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Causality is fraught with difficulties, scientific and how we communicate it. I appreciate the developments in clarifying concepts and assumptions needed for causal inference. item.title: Mind and body approach
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, We would like to thank Barbara Holtzman for her insightful article about chronic pain (BMJ 2026;392:s150). In this article the author eloquently describes her long journey understanding and managing her own pain, eventually finding relief with body based trauma healing. item.title: Re: MyChart: doctors are left frustrated and patients panic as NHS trusts roll out hospital records app
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor It can be very difficult for patients and their families and friends to find out what is happening to their loved ones when they are in hospital. Patients can allow their relatives (or proxies) as well as themselves to see the medical records. Dame Judy Mellor's parliamentary ombudsman report in 2014 showed that a third of complaints were about poor communication. item.title: Benefits of arts and distraction observed within palliative care; a reminder that medicine is more than just ‘’medicines’’
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, It is refreshing to read about non-pharmacological factors that may improve health outcomes, outside the typical pharmacological medicines that us as clinicians often reach for. item.title: Bridging Promise and Evidence in Psychedelic Medicine
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, I read with great interest the recent state-of-the-art review on psychedelic medicine by Jacobs and colleagues, which provides a comprehensive synthesis of the mechanisms, clinical evidence, and translational challenges surrounding psilocybin and 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA) assisted therapies [1]. item.title: The Hepatitis B Birth Dose Trial That Triggered the WHO Alarm
